reason: The wet methane stream needs processing and cold storage for the return fuel, so the methane liquefier seems like a natural first step.
expectation: I expect the liquefier to remove water and cool the methane for storage, though the exact process is unclear.

alternatives.reason: The oxygen also needs its own cold storage; I chose to handle the wet methane first.

effect: The methane is now dry and stored as a liquid, confirming that the plant removes water before liquefaction. Oxygen storage remains.
reaction: The distinction between drying and liquefying the methane was useful to learn.
reason: The oxygen needs its own cold storage, and this is the only available combination.
expectation: I expect the oxygen liquefier to cool the oxygen into a separate liquid store, though I don't know what details the process will show.

effect: The oxygen is now stored separately as a liquid, completing both storage goals and establishing the beginning of a way off Mars.
reaction: The separate stores made the distinction between the fuel and oxidizer clear, though the step was predictable.

mostWorthwhile.text: Processing the wet methane was most worthwhile because it showed that residual water is removed before liquefaction.

leastWorthwhile.text: Storing the oxygen was straightforward and the only remaining combination, so it offered little decision-making.

surprise.text: I learned that the methane stream is dried before it is liquefied for storage.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary; both matched the stated storage goals.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the ice specimen is recovered and brought home, although this chapter itself offered few decisions.
